newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Ito-Yokado hit by food poisoning scare.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Ito-Yokado hit by food poisoning scare.

text.p: A food poisoning scare and a slow economic recovery cut supermarket operator Ito-Yokado Co Ltd's current profits by almost five percent in the first half of the current fiscal year, the company said on Thursday.

The major Japanese supermarket operator said that its parent current profit for the six months to August 31, slumped 4.9 percent from a year ago to 38.66 billion yen ($345 million), while operating revenues grew a scant 1.4 percent to 773.53 billion yen ($6.90 billion) from a year earlier.
Current profits are pre-tax and include losses or gains on non-operating activities such as investments in stocks.
But Seven-Eleven Japan Co Ltd, which was 50.7 percent owned by Ito-Yokado as of the end of February, posted brighter earnings due to stronger sales.

The nation's largest operator of convenience stores said on Thursday that it enjoyed parent current profits of 55.39 billion yen ($494 million) in the same six-month period, up 5.6 percent from its year-ago level.

Ito-Yokado's sales were hit by a food poisoning epidemic that swept Japan earlier this year, triggering health fears about certain fresh foodstuffs, and by an unusually cool summer, which depressed sales of clothing and outdoor goods.

"Our business has been affected by the food poisoning epidemic, but we have suffered less compared with rival stores as we paid close attention to food security," executive vice president Nobutake Sato told reporters.
"But consumption as a whole failed to grow strongly," he said, attributing the trend to a struggling economic recovery which sapped consumer confidence.
But for the full business year to February 28, 1997, the company predicted a parent current profit of 80.5 billion yen ($718 million), up 5.1 percent from a year earlier.
On Tuesday, Japan's largest supermarket chain operator Daiei Inc announced that it had suffered a 49 percent year-on-year drop in its parent current profit for the March-August period.
Seven-Eleven's operating revenues, meanwhile, grew 9.5 percent year-on-year to 128.52 billion yen ($1.14 billion).
It opened a record 266 stores during the half-year period and as of August was operating 6,686 stores.

The firm forecasts current profits of 104 billion yen ($928 million) for the full year to February 28, up six percent from a year earlier, while operating revenues should climb nine percent to 252 billion yen ($2.25 billion). ($1=112 yen)
